howTo: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee and place a resistance band above the knee.

Return to the starting position by driving through the heel of the standing leg and bringing your torso back up.

exercises.description: The Cat/Camel is a gentle movement that involves alternating between arching and rounding the back while on hands and knees.

howTo: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Inhale deeply as you arch your back, lifting your head and tailbone towards the ceiling (Camel position).
Exhale slowly as you round your back, tucking your chin to your chest and drawing your pelvis under (Cat position).
Continue to flow between these two positions, focusing on smooth and controlled movements.
Keep your spine in a neutral position between the extremes of arching and rounding.
commonMistakes: Letting your back sag or arch too much; instead, maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Moving too quickly; focus on controlled and fluid transitions to maximize the benefits.
Neglecting to engage your core; ensure your abdominal muscles are active to support your spine.

exercises.description: Heel Taps are a core exercise performed while lying on your back, where you lower your heels toward the ground and then return them to the starting position.

Tap the heel gently on the ground, then return it to the starting position.
Repeat with the other heel, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Continue alternating heels for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back; focus on pressing your lower back into the ground to maintain proper alignment.
Rushing through the movement; perform each tap slowly and with control to maximize core engagement.

exercises.benefits: The Turkish Get-up may improve functional strength, which is useful for daily activities. It also promotes core stability and shoulder strength, which can enhance overall athletic performance and reduce the risk of injury.
howTo: Lie on your back with one arm extended straight up, holding a weight in that hand.
Bend the knee on the same side as the weight and place your foot flat on the ground.
Use your free hand to push yourself up onto your opposite elbow, then onto your hand.
Lift your hips off the ground and sweep your leg back into a kneeling position.
Stand up by pushing through your front foot and bringing your back leg forward.
Reverse the steps to return to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Not keeping the weight directly above your shoulder; fix this by ensuring your arm is straight and aligned with your shoulder throughout the movement.
Rushing through the steps; focus on moving slowly and deliberately to maintain control and balance.
Allowing the non-weight-bearing leg to drift too far away; keep it close to your body to maintain stability.

exercises.benefits: The Two Leg Pogo may strengthen the calves and improve the elasticity of the lower leg muscles. It can also enhance coordination and stability, contributing to better overall athletic performance.
howTo: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Lift your heels off the ground, balancing on the balls of your feet.
Bounce lightly and quickly, keeping your ankles stiff and landing softly on the midfoot.
Maintain a steady rhythm, ensuring your heels do not touch the ground.
Engage your core to help with balance and stability throughout the movement.
commonMistakes: Landing on the heels; focus on landing midfoot to maintain balance and reduce impact.
Bouncing too high; keep your jumps low and quick for better control and efficiency.
Allowing the ankles to extend; keep your ankles stiff to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise.

exercises.benefits: Strengthening the calves can improve overall lower leg function and may reduce the risk of injuries. This exercise also promotes better balance and coordination, which are essential for daily movements and athletic performance.
howTo: Stand facing a wall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands resting on the wall for support.
Lift your heels off the ground, balancing on the balls of your feet while keeping your knees straight.
Hold this position for the desired time, focusing on engaging your calf muscles.
Lower your heels back to the ground and rest briefly before repeating.
For added challenge, perform the exercise on one leg, keeping the other leg slightly lifted off the ground.
commonMistakes: Raising heels too high; focus on lifting just enough to engage the calves without straining.
Bending the knees; keep your knees straight to properly target the calf muscles.
Leaning too far forward; maintain a straight posture to ensure balance and proper muscle engagement.

exercises.description: Chin-ups are a bodyweight exercise performed by pulling your body up to a bar using your arms and back.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to build upper body strength, particularly in the arms and back. It also enhances grip strength and overall functional fitness.
exercises.benefits: Chin-ups may improve muscular endurance and strength in the upper body, especially the biceps and lats. They can also promote better posture and stability in the shoulders, contributing to overall upper body functionality.
howTo: Grip the pull-up bar with your palms facing you, hands shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended and engage your core.
Pull your body upward until your chin is above the bar, focusing on using your arms and back.
Lower yourself back down to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Rushing the movement; focus on controlled movements to maximize strength gains.
Using momentum to swing up; engage your muscles throughout the movement for better effectiveness.
Not fully extending arms at the bottom; ensure full range of motion for optimal muscle engagement.

exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to strengthen the upper back and improve posture. It can enhance upper body pulling strength, which is beneficial for various activities.
exercises.benefits: The wide grip pulldown may improve muscle endurance and strength in the lats and upper back. It can also help with shoulder stability and may reduce the risk of injury during other upper body exercises.
howTo: Sit at the pulldown machine and adjust the knee pad to secure your legs.
Grip the bar with a wide grip, palms facing away from you.
Engage your core and pull the bar down towards your upper chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, then slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning back too much; keep your torso upright to engage the back muscles effectively.
Using momentum to pull the bar down; focus on a controlled movement to maximize muscle engagement.
Not fully extending the arms; ensure you return the bar to the starting position for a complete range of motion.

exercises.description: The bent-over row is a strength exercise that targets the muscles in your upper back, arms, and shoulders. It involves bending at the hips while pulling weights towards your torso.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is often included in strength training programs to improve upper body strength and posture. It can be performed as part of a super set, which involves alternating between two exercises for increased intensity.
exercises.benefits: The bent-over row may enhance muscle strength and endurance in the upper back and arms. It also promotes better posture by strengthening the muscles that support the spine. Additionally, this exercise can improve overall functional movement, making daily activities easier.
howTo: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Bend at your hips and knees, keeping your back straight and your torso at about a 45-degree angle.
Let your arms hang straight down, palms facing each other.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back; keep your back straight throughout the movement to avoid strain.
Using momentum to lift the weights; focus on using your muscles to pull the weights for better effectiveness.
Not engaging the core; activate your core muscles to support your back and maintain stability during the exercise.

exercises.description: The yoga push-up is a variation of the traditional push-up that combines strength and flexibility. It involves lowering your body while maintaining a straight line from head to heels and then pushing back up.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included to build upper body strength and improve core stability. It also enhances flexibility in the shoulders and chest.
exercises.benefits: The yoga push-up may strengthen the chest, triceps, and core muscles. It promotes better posture and may improve overall functional strength, making daily activities easier.
howTo: Start in a plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Breathe in as you lower down, then exhale as you push back up to the starting position.
Maintain control throughout the movement, focusing on smooth, steady motions.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag; keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Rushing the movement; focus on controlled lowering and pushing to enhance strength.
Not engaging the core; tighten your abdominal muscles to stabilize your body during the exercise.

Step backward, focusing on keeping your core engaged.

Not engaging the core; keep your core tight to enhance stability and support your lower back.

howTo: Sit or lie down comfortably on your back with your legs extended.

Relax and repeat for the recommended number of sets.

exercises.benefits: Strengthening the calves can improve overall lower leg function and may reduce the risk of injuries related to the ankle and foot. This exercise also contributes to better performance in activities that involve running, jumping, and climbing.

Lower your heel back down to the ground in a controlled manner.

Not fully extending the ankle; ensure you push through the ball of your foot as you lift.

exercises.description: The single-leg pogo in place is a balance and strength exercise performed on one leg, focusing on quick, light bounces.

howTo: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in your knee and your core engaged.
Lift your opposite foot off the ground and maintain a tall posture.
Bounce lightly on the ball of your standing foot, keeping your movements quick and controlled.

Switch legs after a set time or number of bounces.

Bouncing too hard; focus on light, quick bounces to enhance control and stability.

exercises.description: The Single-Leg Pogo Side to Side is a dynamic exercise that involves jumping from side to side on one leg.

exercises.benefits: Performing this exercise may strengthen the glutes and calves, contributing to better overall lower body function. It can also improve balance, which is important for daily activities and sports performance.
howTo: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in your knee and engage your core.
Push off the ground with your foot and jump sideways to the opposite side.
Land softly on the same leg, maintaining balance and control.
Immediately push off again to jump back to the starting side.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, focusing on keeping your hips level.

Not engaging the core; activate your core muscles to support stability during the jumps.

exercises.description: The single-leg squat to bench is a balance and strength exercise performed on one leg, lowering your body to a bench or similar surface.
exercises.purpose: This exercise enhances lower body strength and stability, particularly in the quads and glutes. It also improves balance and coordination, which are essential for various physical activities.
exercises.benefits: Single-leg squats may increase strength in the legs and improve joint stability. They may also enhance balance and coordination, helping to prevent falls and injuries during daily activities.
howTo: Stand on one leg in front of a bench or sturdy surface.
Engage your core and keep your chest up.
Bend your knee and lower your body toward the bench, keeping your knee aligned over your toes.
Lightly touch the bench with your glutes, then push through your heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
commonMistakes: Knee caves in; focus on keeping your knee aligned over your toes throughout the movement.
Leaning forward; maintain an upright chest to support your balance and engage your core.
Not using a bench; start with a bench or surface to ensure safety and control as you lower.

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.description: The barbell deadlift is a strength exercise that involves lifting a barbell from the ground to hip level while maintaining a straight back.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in programs to build overall strength and power, particularly in the lower body and back. It also helps improve functional movement patterns used in daily activities.
exercises.benefits: The deadlift may enhance muscle strength in the legs, back, and core. It also promotes better posture and stability, which can improve performance in other exercises and daily tasks. Additionally, it may increase metabolic rate due to the large muscle groups involved.
howTo: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, with the barbell positioned over the middle of your feet.
Bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with both hands, keeping your back straight.
Engage your core and push through your heels to lift the barbell, extending your hips and knees simultaneously.
Stand tall at the top of the lift, ensuring your shoulders are back and your chest is up.
Lower the barbell back to the ground by bending at your hips and knees, maintaining a straight back throughout the movement.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back: Keep your back straight and chest up to avoid strain on your spine.
Lifting with the arms: Focus on using your legs and hips to lift the weight, not your arms.
Not engaging the core: Tighten your core muscles before lifting to provide stability and support.

exercises.name: Cardio Choice (Active Recovery)
exercises.description: Active recovery involves engaging in low-intensity cardiovascular activities, such as walking, cycling, or swimming, to promote recovery between more intense workouts.
exercises.purpose: Including active recovery in a program helps to maintain blood flow to the muscles, which can aid in recovery and reduce soreness. It also allows individuals to stay active while giving their body a break from high-intensity training.
exercises.benefits: Active recovery may enhance circulation, helping to deliver nutrients to muscles and remove waste products. This can lead to improved recovery times and overall performance in subsequent workouts. It also promotes mental well-being by keeping you engaged in physical activity without the stress of high intensity.
howTo: Choose a low-intensity activity that you enjoy, such as walking, cycling, or swimming.
Engage in the activity for 20 to 30 minutes at a comfortable pace.
Focus on your breathing and maintain a steady rhythm throughout the session.
Stay hydrated and listen to your body; stop if you feel any discomfort.
Incorporate this into your weekly routine, ideally after more intense workout days.
commonMistakes: Choosing too intense of an activity; instead, select a lower intensity to truly allow for recovery.
Neglecting hydration; remember to drink water before, during, and after your session.
Skipping the warm-up; always start with a few minutes of gentle movement to prepare your body.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Forward Lunge
exercises.description: The dumbbell forward lunge is a lower body exercise where you step forward with one leg while holding a dumbbell in each hand.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to enhance leg strength, stability, and balance. It also engages the core for additional support.
exercises.benefits: The dumbbell forward lunge may improve overall leg strength by targeting the quads, hamstrings, and glutes. It can also enhance balance and coordination, which are important for daily activities and sports.
howTo: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides.
Step forward with your right leg, lowering your body until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat on the left leg, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward; keep your torso upright to maintain balance and protect your back.
Letting the front knee extend past the toes; ensure your knee stays aligned over your ankle for proper form.
Not engaging the core; activate your core muscles to support your lower back and maintain stability.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Military Press
exercises.description: The seated barbell military press is a strength exercise performed while sitting, using a barbell to press overhead.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to build upper body strength, particularly in the shoulders and arms. It also helps improve stability and posture.
exercises.benefits: Performing the seated barbell military press may enhance muscle strength in the shoulders and triceps. It can also improve core stability as the body works to maintain an upright position. Additionally, it may increase overall upper body power, which is beneficial for various physical activities.
howTo: Sit on a bench with back support and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lift the barbell to shoulder height, keeping your elbows directly below your wrists.
Engage your core and press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the barbell back to shoulder height in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Arching the back; keep your back pressed against the bench to maintain stability.
Using momentum to lift the bar; focus on controlled movements to engage the muscles effectively.
Letting the elbows flare out; keep them close to your body to target the shoulders properly.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: The dumbbell reverse lunge is a lower body exercise where you step back into a lunge while holding dumbbells at your sides.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to improve leg strength and stability. It also enhances balance and coordination.
exercises.benefits: Performing reverse lunges may strengthen the quads, hamstrings, and glutes. This exercise can also improve functional movement patterns, making daily activities easier and safer.
howTo: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step back with one foot, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at about a 90-degree angle.
Keep your front knee aligned over your ankle and your back knee hovering just above the ground.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Alternate legs with each repetition.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee extend past the toes; keep the knee aligned over the ankle for better stability.
Leaning forward; maintain an upright torso to engage the core and protect your back.
Not stepping back far enough; ensure you create enough distance to lower into the lunge properly.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.description: A bodyweight squat is a lower body exercise that involves bending the knees and lowering the body as if sitting back into a chair, then returning to a standing position.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to build strength in the legs and improve overall mobility. It also engages the core for stability.
exercises.benefits: Bodyweight squats may enhance leg strength, particularly in the quads, hamstrings, and glutes. They can also improve balance and flexibility in the hips and ankles, contributing to better functional movement in daily activities.
howTo: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly pointed outward.
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you begin to bend your knees.
Lower your body down as if sitting back into a chair, keeping your weight on your heels.
Go down until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as comfortable.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward too much; keep your chest up and back straight to maintain balance.
Letting the knees collapse inward; push your knees outward to align them with your toes.
Not going low enough; aim to lower your thighs parallel to the ground for maximum benefit.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: The bodyweight reverse lunge is a lower body exercise where you step back into a lunge position and return to standing.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to improve leg strength, balance, and coordination. It also helps enhance hip and knee mobility.
exercises.benefits: Performing reverse lunges may strengthen the quads, hamstrings, and glutes. It can also improve stability and functional movement patterns, which are important for daily activities.
howTo: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step back with your right foot, lowering your body until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Keep your chest up and core engaged as you lower down.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side, stepping back with your left foot.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward; keep your chest upright to maintain balance.
Letting your front knee go past your toes; ensure your knee stays aligned with your ankle.
Not engaging your core; activate your core muscles to support your lower back.

exercises.name: Prone Superman Reverse Fly
exercises.description: The prone Superman reverse fly is an exercise performed while lying face down, lifting your arms out to the sides to engage the upper back and shoulder muscles.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to strengthen the upper back and improve posture. It also enhances shoulder stability and mobility.
exercises.benefits: Strengthening the upper back may improve posture and reduce the risk of shoulder injuries. This exercise also engages the muscles that support the spine, promoting better alignment and overall stability.
howTo: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
Lift your arms and chest off the ground while keeping your legs and hips in contact with the mat.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together as you raise your arms to form a 'T' shape.
Hold the position for a moment, then lower your arms and chest back to the mat.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Lifting the arms without engaging the back; focus on squeezing the shoulder blades together to activate the upper back.
Arching the lower back excessively; keep your hips and legs grounded to maintain a neutral spine.
Raising the arms too high; aim to lift to shoulder height to avoid straining the shoulders.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Forward Lunge
exercises.description: The bodyweight forward lunge is a lower body exercise where you step forward with one leg and lower your body until both knees are bent at about a 90-degree angle.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to improve leg strength, balance, and coordination. It also helps enhance flexibility in the hips and legs.
exercises.benefits: Performing forward lunges may improve functional movement patterns, making daily activities easier. It strengthens the quads, hamstrings, and glutes, which can contribute to better overall lower body strength and stability.
howTo: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step forward with your right leg, lowering your body until your right knee is directly above your ankle and your left knee nearly touches the ground.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat on the left side, stepping forward with your left leg.
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee extend past the toes; keep the knee aligned over the ankle for better stability.
Leaning forward; maintain an upright torso to engage the core and protect your back.
Not lowering enough; aim for both knees to reach about 90 degrees for maximum effectiveness.

exercises.name: Lateral Arm Circles
exercises.description: Lateral arm circles are a simple exercise where you move your arms in small circles to the side while standing or sitting.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included to improve shoulder mobility and strengthen the muscles around the shoulder joint. It can also enhance coordination and stability in the upper body.
exercises.benefits: Lateral arm circles may improve shoulder flexibility and endurance. They can strengthen the shoulder muscles, which may reduce the risk of injury during other activities. This exercise also promotes better posture by engaging the upper back and shoulder stabilizers.
howTo: Stand or sit with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended to the sides at shoulder height.
Keep your arms straight and begin to make small circles with your arms, moving them forward.
Gradually increase the size of the circles while maintaining control.
After a set time or number of repetitions, switch direction and make circles backward.
Continue for the same duration or repetitions in the opposite direction.
commonMistakes: Moving too quickly; slow down to maintain control and ensure proper form.
Bending the elbows; keep your arms straight to effectively engage the shoulder muscles.
Raising the shoulders; relax your shoulders down away from your ears to avoid tension.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Single Leg Deadlift
exercises.description: The bodyweight single leg deadlift is an exercise that targets the muscles in your legs and core while improving balance and stability. It involves bending forward on one leg while keeping the other leg extended behind you.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to enhance strength and coordination in the lower body. It also helps develop balance, which is important for overall functional movement.
exercises.benefits: Performing this exercise may strengthen the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. It can also improve your balance and stability, which may enhance performance in other physical activities.
howTo: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Hinge at the hips, lowering your torso while extending the other leg straight back.
Keep your back straight and core engaged as you lower down.
Return to the starting position by driving through the standing heel and bringing your torso back up.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
commonMistakes: Leaning too far forward; keep your back straight and hinge at the hips instead.
Bending the standing knee too much; maintain a slight bend to keep balance.
Not engaging the core; tighten your core muscles to support your lower back.
Rushing through the movement; perform the exercise slowly and with control for better balance.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL with Foam Roll Adduction

demos.notes: Single Leg RDL with Foam Roll Adduction

metadata.title: Single Leg RDL with Foam Roll Adduction

recommendations.note: Squeeze a foam roller between the thighs to cue adduction and balance. Move slowly and keep the standing knee soft.

exercises.description: The single-leg RDL with foam roll adduction is a single-leg hip hinge performed while lightly squeezing a foam roller between the thighs. You hinge at the hip on one leg while the other leg extends behind you.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to train the posterior chain and single-leg balance while the foam roller cue engages the inner thigh. It builds control through the hip and knee, which supports rehab of the lower body.
exercises.benefits: Performing this exercise may strengthen the hamstrings, glutes, and adductors while improving balance and hip stability. The added adduction cue can support better alignment of the knee over the foot.
howTo: Stand on one leg and place a foam roller between your thighs.
Hinge at the hip and lower your torso as the free leg extends behind you.
Keep your back flat and gently squeeze the roller throughout.
Drive through the standing heel to return to standing.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back as you hinge. Keep your chest open and hinge from the hips.
Locking the standing knee. Keep a slight bend to protect the joint and hold balance.
Rushing the movement. Move slowly to keep control and feel the working muscles.

exercises.name: Goblet Cossack Squat

metadata.title: Goblet Cossack squat
metadata.channel: CrossFit Monarch X Functional strength training

recommendations.note: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest. Shift side to side and keep the trailing leg straight with the foot flat.

exercises.description: The goblet Cossack squat is a lateral squat where you hold a weight at your chest and shift your weight onto one bent leg while the other stays straight. It moves the body side to side rather than straight down.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to build lateral strength, hip and ankle mobility, and single-leg control. It trains the adductors and glutes through a wide range of motion.
exercises.benefits: Performing this exercise may improve hip and ankle mobility, strengthen the quads, glutes, and inner thighs, and support better side-to-side stability. The goblet load helps you stay upright and balanced.
howTo: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest and stand with a wide stance.
Shift your weight onto one leg and bend that knee while keeping the other leg straight.
Keep both feet flat and your chest tall at the bottom.
Press through the bent leg to return to center, then repeat on the other side.
commonMistakes: Letting the heel of the bent leg lift. Sit back and keep the foot flat for a stable base.
Rounding forward. Hold the weight close and keep your chest up to stay upright.
Collapsing the knee inward. Track the knee over the toes as you lower.

exercises.name: GHD Hip Extension

recommendations.note: Hinge only at the hips, not the lower back. Rise until your body forms a straight line and pause briefly at the top.

exercises.description: The GHD hip extension is performed on a glute-ham developer, where you hinge at the hips and raise your torso from a bent position to a straight line. The knees stay mostly extended so the movement comes from the hips.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to strengthen the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back through a controlled hip hinge. It reinforces the posterior chain pattern used in many lower-body movements.
exercises.benefits: Performing this exercise may strengthen the glutes, hamstrings, and spinal erectors and improve control of the hip hinge. Stronger posterior-chain muscles can support the lower back during daily movement.
howTo: Set up on the glute-ham developer with your hips at the pad edge.
Lower your torso by hinging at the hips with a flat back.
Squeeze your glutes to raise your body into a straight line.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower under control.
commonMistakes: Arching or rounding the lower back. Keep a neutral spine and move from the hips.
Swinging up with momentum. Rise slowly and squeeze the glutes to lift.
Overextending at the top. Stop at a straight line rather than arching past it.

exercises.name: Banded Knee Drive

recommendations.note: Loop a band around both feet and lie on your back. Drive both knees toward your chest together, then lower with control.

exercises.description: The banded knee drive is a floor exercise where you lie on your back with a resistance band looped around both feet and pull both knees toward your chest at the same time. The band adds resistance as your hips and core work to draw the knees in.
exercises.purpose: This exercise is included in a program to train the hip flexors and deep core through a controlled knee-to-chest motion. It supports the hip drive used in running and other lower-body movement.
exercises.benefits: Performing this exercise may strengthen the hip flexors and core and improve control of the hips against resistance. Stronger hip flexors can support knee drive and stride mechanics.
howTo: Lie on your back and loop a resistance band around both feet.
Start with your legs extended and the band under light tension.
Draw both knees toward your chest together against the band.
Lower your legs back to the start under control.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back off the floor. Press your lower back down and brace your core.
Yanking the knees in with momentum. Move slowly so the hips and core do the work.
Holding your breath. Exhale as you draw the knees in and breathe steadily.
